security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by animation documentation, JavaScript template literals, example URLs, and test utilities. The audit confirmed a dependency-provenance risk: environment-controlled module search paths feed a dynamic import, and the fallback bootstrap can install @latest. No prompt injection, secret collection, covert exfiltration, or screen-capture upload behavior was found. Static review was capped at 400/648 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 248 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: The dependency bootstrap falls back to @latest when it cannot determine a bundled version.
remediation.suggestion: Fail closed when the version is unavailable, or require an explicit exact version through HYPERFRAMES_SKILL_PKG_VERSION before installing.

remediation.issue: Environment and PATH-derived module directories can control the entry passed to dynamic import.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve packages only from the project root and the temporary bootstrap directory, then verify package names, real paths, and expected versions before import.

remediation.issue: Temporary package installation executes newly downloaded package code when the process is restarted.
remediation.suggestion: Document this trust boundary clearly and add integrity verification or a lockfile-based exact package source for bootstrap dependencies.

content.value_statement: Building multi-phase animation scenes can require many timing and runtime decisions. This skill provides focused motion recipes, blueprints, and an animation-map review workflow for HyperFrames projects.
actual_capabilities: Select and combine atomic GSAP motion rules for HyperFrames scenes.
Provide multi-phase scene blueprints for interfaces, brands, metrics, and text.
Explain seek-safe animation constraints and deterministic timeline practices.
Offer runtime-specific guidance for GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, CSS, WAAPI, and TypeGPU.
Generate animation-map reports that identify tween timing, staggers, and dead zones.
limitations: It is designed for HyperFrames composition conventions and may need adaptation for other frameworks.
The animation-map script requires a runnable composition and compatible helper packages.
Example assets and external runtime libraries may require separate installation or network access.
The skill provides design guidance, not final visual approval or accessibility testing.

use_cases.title: Build a product interface reveal
use_cases.description: Combine cursor, card, counter, and press rules into a timed product demonstration.

use_cases.title: Plan a branded motion sequence
use_cases.description: Start from a multi-phase blueprint and tailor its timing, typography, and scene transitions.

use_cases.title: Review animation choreography
use_cases.description: Run the animation-map workflow to inspect tween coverage, stagger timing, and inactive periods.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a motion rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest two HyperFrames animation rules for a headline that enters, settles, and remains readable. Explain the order and timing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a UI scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a seek-safe HyperFrames GSAP timeline for a dashboard card that reveals a metric, counts up, and highlights a final action.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the cursor UI demo blueprint for a 6-second product workflow. List phases, selected rules, timeline labels, and deterministic constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit choreography
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to run animation-map on my HyperFrames composition. Then help interpret dead zones, stagger notes, and lifecycle warnings from its report.

output_examples.input: Create a short product metric reveal.
output: Suggested sequence: card entry, metric count-up, then a brief emphasis on the result.
Timeline notes: use one paused timeline and explicit labels for each phase.
Animation-map workflow: generate a local report from registered GSAP timelines.
Review focus: long inactive intervals, inconsistent staggers, and unusually short tweens.

best_practices: Use one paused timeline with explicit labels and a defined scene duration.
Select only the rules needed for the story, then test the composition at several seek positions.
Pin helper package versions when running the animation-map script outside a bundled installation.
anti_patterns: Do not create infinite or time-dependent animation loops in a deterministic composition.
Do not mix unrelated motion rules without a clear phase order or visual purpose.
Do not treat animation-map output as a substitute for visual and accessibility review.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create and review deterministic HyperFrames animations using rules, blueprints, and runtime guidance.

faq.question: Which animation runtime is the default?
faq.answer: GSAP is the default runtime for most atomic motion rules in this skill.

faq.question: Can I use Lottie or Three.js?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes adapter guidance for Lottie, Three.js, CSS, WAAPI, Anime.js, and TypeGPU.

faq.question: What is animation-map?
faq.answer: It is a local script that reads registered GSAP timelines and produces a choreography report.

faq.question: Does animation-map change my composition?
faq.answer: It writes its report to the selected output directory and uses a temporary bundled capture directory.

faq.question: How should I manage helper dependencies?
faq.answer: Prefer project-installed, pinned packages. Review and approve any temporary bootstrap prompt before installation.
